title: Functoriality of the conormal sheaf of a closed immersion
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ and $i':Z'\to X'$ be closed immersions of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaves $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ and $\mathcal I'=\ker(\mathcal O_{X'}\to i'_*\mathcal O_{Z'})$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and call $\mathcal C_{Z/X}:=i^*\mathcal I\;(=i^*(\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2))$ and $\mathcal C_{Z'/X'}:=i'^*\mathcal I'$ their conormal sheaves [def-pc-module-pullback], where $\mathcal I^2$ denotes the subsheaf generated by products of two local sections of $\mathcal I$. Let $g:X\to X'$ and $f:Z\to Z'$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $g\circ i=i'\circ f$. Then (1) the image $\mathcal I'\mathcal O_X$ of $g^*\mathcal I'\to g^*\mathcal O_{X'}\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is contained in $\mathcal I$, so $g^\sharp$ induces an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\gamma:g^*\mathcal I'\to\mathcal I$; (2) the composite $c:f^*\mathcal C_{Z'/X'}=f^*i'^*\mathcal I'\cong i^*g^*\mathcal I'\xrightarrow{i^*\gamma}i^*\mathcal I=\mathcal C_{Z/X}$ is a canonical map of $\mathcal O_Z$-modules, characterized by: for affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X$, $U'=\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset X'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $g(U)\subset U'$, $Z\cap U=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$, $Z'\cap U'=\operatorname{Spec}(R'/I')$, the induced map $I'/I'^2=\Gamma(Z'\cap U',\mathcal C_{Z'/X'})\to\Gamma(Z\cap U,\mathcal C_{Z/X})=I/I^2$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-conormal-sections] is induced by $g^\sharp:R'\to R$, which satisfies $g^\sharp(I')\subset I$.

proof.text: Use IdealSheafData.le_map_iff_comap_le and map_ker to rewrite ideal containment as i′.ker ≤ (i ≫ g).ker. Rewrite by the square equality and apply Hom.le_ker_comp to f and i′. This uses only the ideal-sheaf Galois connection and the kernel of a composite.

The existing source-library map IdealSheafData.pullbackToModulesι g J has zero composite with the quotient by J.comap g (pullbackToModulesι_comp_toPushforwardSubscheme). Kernel.lift therefore factors it through (J.comap g).toModules. The containment from step 1 and inclusion_subschemeι show that the inclusion of this ideal has zero composite with i.ker.toPushforwardSubscheme; a second kernel lift corestricts into i.ker.toModules. Compare tensorPullback g with Mathlib pullback g using Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq. Its unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app equation, together with pullbackToModulesι_app_unit, proves the required formula for γ on every open.

Compose the chosen tensor-pullback adjunctions along i′ and f. Transport their composite right adjoint through pushforwardComp f i′ and pushforwardCongr h.symm. Apply the inverse Hom equivalence of this adjunction to the morphism obtained from γ and the units along g and i. Adjunction.comp_homEquiv, homEquiv_ofNatIsoRight_apply and homEquiv_unit give precisely the adjoint equality in the statement. Injectivity of that Hom equivalence proves uniqueness from this equality alone.

For U ⊆ g⁻¹(U′), take s to be the restriction to U of γ applied to the g-pullback unit of s′. Naturality of i.ker.toModulesι and the section formula from step 2 give i.ker.toModulesι(s) = g.appLE(s′). Evaluate the adjoint equality from step 3 on s′; pushforwardComp acts as the identity on sections. Naturality of the i-pullback unit under restriction gives the final affine equation. This argument works on arbitrary opens and does not need affine quotient calculations or tensor generators. No unit-level realization is bypassed: this node is not among sk-thm-p1.realized.
